originalText:
Hey all! 

Please upgrade to 5.0 by clicking on the button on the top left of the app's window if you're a regular user, I'm really proud of this update :)

And if you've tried Ghostex before but had any issues with performance or bugs then I hope you try this new version because it's honestly much better! 

I just released 5.0 today and it's the biggest jump in performance and features  in all the past releases.

You should notice that all of these are much faster now: 

1. Switching between warm terminals and warm views (source/browser/kanban/docs) is instant now and the delay is fully gone. 

2. The sidebar scroll area is much lighter and smoother to scroll and reacts instantly compared to before.

3. The Kanban board actions were optimized heavily (local first design which syncs with the beads db).

(Warm means they aren't sleeping to conserve resources) 

There's also a new project view called docs that combines: 
1. The Claude app's ″Artifacts″ feature
2. With Excalidraw
3. Plus Plannonator's md files annotation features :)

Just tell your agent to create or edit one of these in the docs folder: 
- A new html prototype/explainer
- An excalidraw drawing
- An md plan or PRD doc

You'll be able to collaborate with the agent very well because of this feature and being able to annotate & ask for edits or even by just editing things yourself and asking the agent to read the edits :) 

Other important things:
- Fully ported the backend logic for gxserver bg service to Rust for better performance than the old TypeScript code. 

- Released an easier to navigate settings modal

- Fixed a ton of bugs

- Made Android & iOS apps auto scale the terminal on connect

- Merged the ability to set any dock/switcher icon you want for the app while it's running (first PR by the app's biggest supporter @Nite_I_Am!)   

- Added instructions on how to use computer use and browser use.

- Made a ton of progress on the port from macOS swift/appkit to Rust/GPUI (Zed IDE's fast framework) which would let this app run on windows and linux (need contributors to help, this is a huge undertaking :)
+ Much more

I didn't even realize it, but my app has already been released..?! Anyway, this is the very first time in my life officially launching an app, so yeah—it feels pretty good.

But I'm actually uploading a new version with some bug fixes right now, so you can wait and download the next version when it's out. Or you can just try it out now, since it's not like a huge game-breaking bug or anything.

Anyway, I ended up revealing my real name too… um, yeah. But anyway, I'm planning to release this app on all other operating systems as well, like iOS, Android, Windows, Linux, etc.

The reason I made this app is simple: I just wanted a social media-style notepad. There is a way to do that—you could just make a Twitter account and set it to private. But even then, it doesn't completely solve privacy concerns because the data is still stored externally.

With this app, everything is saved right on your device, so you don't have to worry about that at all. I made it as comfortable as possible for myself to use, while giving it a vibe similar to social media like Twitter.

If you had the same need as me, I think you'll really like it!

🍎Lifetime: $39.99 → Free 🍎

You know that feeling when you want a puzzle that actually makes you think...

But not one that's screaming for your attention with flashing rewards, countdown timers, and twelve different currencies?

Sometimes you just want a quiet challenge.

That’s exactly what Lexoku delivers.

Lexoku takes the satisfying logic of Sudoku and gives it a clever twist: instead of numbers, you're working with letters from a word.

Maybe it's a five-letter word like BRAIN. Maybe it's something longer like HARMONY.

Your goal is simple: place the letters into the grid so every row and column contains the exact letters of the word at the correct frequency.

Sounds easy.

Then suddenly you're twenty minutes deep, staring at one square and questioning everything.

A few reasons puzzle fans are loving it:
• Daily Challenge with a fresh puzzle every day
• Game Center leaderboards to compare solve times
• Weekly themed puzzle packs released every Monday
• Over 6,000 hand-curated puzzles
• Multiple difficulty levels whenever you want them
• No timers forcing you to rush
• No vocabulary tests or trivia knowledge required
• Relaxing, single-player experience built around pure logic

What makes Lexoku special is how calm it feels.

No pressure. No punishment. No losing streaks.

Just one more puzzle... and then somehow another one after that.

If you enjoy Sudoku, word games, logic puzzles, or simply having something thoughtful to unwind with, this one is dangerously easy to get hooked on.

Quietly addictive is probably the perfect description.
